summary: This article covers an overview of the many events in track and field, from sprints and distance races to hurdles, jumps, and throws, and the different skills each one demands.
introduce: Draw two overlapping circles on the board and quickly compare two familiar things, such as a cat and a dog, with the class. Tell students that while reading “Track and Field: Running, Jumping, Throwing” they will look for ways things are alike and different.

keyTerms.def: how far something travels, or a long race
a race in which team members take turns covering part of the distance
a small barrier that a runner must jump over while racing

challengeTerms.def: the speed of something in a particular direction
the force a moving body has that keeps it moving
the curved path an object follows through the air

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that it is better to specialize in one track and field event than to try many different ones? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the skills needed for a sprint are different from the skills needed for a throwing event like the shot put.
struggling: Pre-teach distance, relay, and hurdle with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses velocity, momentum, and trajectory to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
